topic: Who invented the parachute? (history explainer, host Nea Costel)
title: WHO INVENTED THE
PARACHUTE?

script.text: Who invented the parachute? Leonardo da Vinci? Sure, he drew one. Around 1485.
Paris, 1797. André-Jacques Garnerin goes up in a hydrogen balloon.
About nine hundred metres up, he cuts the rope.
The basket swings like crazy. But he lands. Alive.
The first parachute jump in history.
And Leonardo's design? In 2000, a skydiver built it from wood and canvas. It worked. He still cut away and landed on a modern chute.

science.claim: Leonardo da Vinci sketched a pyramid parachute around 1485 but never tested it.
Garnerin made the first recorded parachute descent from a balloon on 22 October 1797 over Parc Monceau, Paris, from about 900 m; the basket swung violently.
science.working: Guinness gives ~914 m (3,000 ft); Smithsonian Air & Space gives 2,000 ft; script says about 900 m.
science.source: Guinness World Records; Smithsonian Air & Space; Wikipedia

science.claim: In 2000 Adrian Nicholas jumped with a replica of Leonardo’s design (wood and canvas) over South Africa; it worked, but he cut away at about 600 m and landed on a conventional parachute.
